# Lua API reference (auto-generated)

Generated by `tools/gen_lua_api.py` from the `///` doc strings in `src/script/api_*.cpp`.
Do not edit by hand; re-run the generator after API changes. Every function must carry a
`/// table.name(args) -> ret | description` line above its handler (or reg() call).

## scene

### `scene.entity(name?: string) -> entity`

create a new entity, optionally named

### `scene.emplace(e: entity, type: string, fields?: table)`

create or replace component `type` on e from a field table (a Geometry table may carry a "shapes" array)

### `scene.replace(e: entity, type: string, fields?: table)`

replace an existing component `type` on e from a field table (errors if the component is absent; Geometry may carry "shapes")

### `scene.component(e: entity, type: string) -> table`

read component `type` from e as a field table (nil if absent or unknown type)

### `scene.remove(e: entity, type: string)`

remove component `type` from e (errors if absent or unknown type)

### `scene.set_pose(e: entity|string, pos: vec3, quat: quat)`

set the local Transform of e (errors if e has no Transform)

### `scene.get_pose(e: entity|string) -> table`

local Transform of e as {pos = {x,y,z}, quat = {x,y,z,w}} (errors if e has no Transform)

### `scene.world_pose(e: entity|string) -> table`

world-space pose of e as {pos = {x,y,z}, quat = {x,y,z,w}}; live Transform+Parent walk, always current (unlike the per-substep WorldTransform snapshot)

### `scene.set_morph(e: entity|string, name: string, weight: number)`

set the blend weight of shape key `name`; on a skinned character (no Geometry) it applies to all linked meshes

### `scene.shapes(e: entity|string) -> table`

shape keys of mesh e as an array of {name, weight} (errors if e has no Geometry)

### `scene.link_mesh(skel: entity|string, mesh: entity|string)`

attach mesh to skeleton skel's skinned meshes (errors if skel has no Skeleton)

### `scene.get_entity(name: string) -> entity`

look up a named entity (nil if not found)

### `scene.find_components(component: string, root?: entity) -> table`

every entity in root's subtree carrying `component` (all top-level entities when root is omitted), as an array of entities

### `scene.attach_script(e: entity, file: string, params?: table)`

attach (or re-attach, replacing any existing script) a Lua module to e; `params` is passed to its _on_ready

### `scene.destroy(e: entity)`

destroy e and its whole subtree; errors if e is a shape referenced by a collider, a texture referenced by a material, or a geometry referenced by a renderable outside the subtree

### `scene.add_child(parent: entity, child: entity, opts?: table)`

reparent child under parent (parent needs a Transform); opts.keepWorld = true re-expresses the child's local pose so its world position is unchanged

### `scene.set(target: entity|string, field: string, value: number|table)`

set a reflected field (URL form "Entity.field" or entity + field name); value is a number or an array of up to 4 numbers

### `scene.get(target: entity|string, field?: string) -> number`

vec3|vec4 | read a reflected field (URL form "Entity.field", or entity + field name); returns a scalar, {x,y,z}, or {x,y,z,w} depending on the field's width

### `scene.time() -> number`

seconds since engine start (monotonic, for _animate timing)

### `scene.button(name: string, fn: function)`

register a named button callback; fired by ui.fire_button(name) or a UI widget bound to that action

### `scene.scenes() -> table`

list loadable scenes in assets/scenes as an array of {label, path} (label from the json "name" field when present)

### `scene.request_scene(path: string)`

queue a scene to load at the end of this frame (e.g. from a UI button)

### `scene.last_error() -> string`

error message from the last failed scene load (empty when none)

## math

_Vector/quaternion helpers added on top of Lua's standard `math` library_

### `math.vadd(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> vec3`

vector addition

### `math.vsub(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> vec3`

vector subtraction

### `math.vscale(v: vec3, s: number) -> vec3`

scalar multiplication

### `math.vlen(v: vec3) -> number`

Euclidean length of v

### `math.vnorm(v: vec3) -> vec3`

unit-length (normalized) copy of v

### `math.vcross(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> vec3`

cross product a x b

### `math.vdot(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> number`

dot product a . b

### `math.qmul(a: quat, b: quat) -> quat`

quaternion product a * b (apply b first, then a)

### `math.qinv(q: quat) -> quat`

inverse (conjugate) of q

### `math.qaxis(axis: vec3, angle: number) -> quat`

axis-angle to quaternion (angle in radians; axis is normalized internally)

### `math.qrot(q: quat, v: vec3) -> vec3`

rotate vector v by quaternion q

### `math.qfromto(a: vec3, b: vec3) -> quat`

shortest rotation mapping direction a onto b

## graphics

### `graphics.gltf(e: entity, path: string) -> entity`

load a glTF file into e (meshes, materials, textures, skeleton); returns e

### `graphics.load_texture(path: string, name?: string) -> entity`

create a path-only Texture (file loaded and uploaded on first use), optionally named

### `graphics.render_texture(w: int, h: int, name?: string) -> entity`

create a standalone GPUTexture render target (no Texture parent); render into it, then attach to a material or environment (errors when the graphics server is disabled)

## physics

### `physics.raycast(origin: vec3, dir: vec3, maxDist: number, excludes?: table) -> table`

rigid-body raycast; returns {hit = true, pos = vec3, dist = number, entity = entity} or nil when nothing is hit; `excludes` is an array of entities to skip

## soft

### `soft.set_floor(y: number)`

set the Y of the soft-body (cloth) floor plane (errors when the graphics server is disabled)

## ui

### `ui.window(title: string, w?: number, h?: number) -> entity`

create a UI canvas window (default 320x200) at a fixed world spot in front of the default view; re-place via the canvas Transform

### `ui.tab(win: entity, label: string) -> entity`

add a tab page to window win

### `ui.editor(tab: entity)`

fill tab with the scene editor (entity tree + reflected field widgets for every selected entity)

### `ui.button(parent: entity, label: string, fn: function) -> entity`

add a button under parent; fn is called when it is clicked

### `ui.text(parent: entity, label: string) -> entity`

add a static text line under parent

### `ui.section(parent: entity, label: string, collapsible?: bool) -> entity`

add a (collapsible by default) labeled section under parent; its children are added to the returned entity

### `ui.slider_f(parent: entity, label: string, bind: string, lo?: number, hi?: number, fmt?: string) -> entity`

add a float slider under parent bound to reflected field `bind` (lo/hi default to the field's own range; fmt defaults to "%.2f")

### `ui.slider_i(parent: entity, label: string, bind: string, lo?: number, hi?: number) -> entity`

add an integer slider under parent bound to reflected field `bind` (lo/hi default to the field's own range)

### `ui.checkbox(parent: entity, label: string, bind: string) -> entity`

add a checkbox under parent bound to reflected bool field `bind`

### `ui.color(parent: entity, label: string, bind: string) -> entity`

add a color picker under parent bound to reflected vec3 field `bind` (RGB 0..1)

### `ui.drag_v3(parent: entity, label: string, bind: string, speed?: number) -> entity`

add a 3D drag gizmo under parent bound to reflected vec3 field `bind` (default move speed 0.1)

### `ui.fire_button(name: string)`

fire a named button callback registered via scene.button(name, fn)

## input

### `input.key_down(kb: entity, code: number) -> bool`

true if key `code` is held on the KeyboardInput entity kb (false for out-of-range codes)

## script hooks (attached modules)

_A `.lua` file attached via `scene.attach_script(e, file, params)` must return a table (the module). The engine calls its hooks with a per-attach instance table as `self`._

### `inst` — per-attach instance table passed as self to every hook; fields: entity (the attached entity), params (the table passed to scene.attach_script, when given); its __index metatable is the module, so module functions act as methods and inst fields hold per-instance state

### `_on_ready(inst)`

called once when the attached module has loaded

### `_animate(inst, dt)`

called every frame with the frame delta time in seconds

### `_physics(inst, dt)`

called every fixed physics step (120 Hz) before the Jolt step; the place to write kinematic poses
